Ingredient.title: Ingredient
Ingredient.description: Represents an individual food ingredient with its pricing information and standard unit of measure for efficient cost calculation in recipes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Ingredient entity.

name.description: The common name of the ingredient (e.g., 'Tomato', 'Chicken Breast').

description.description: A brief description or additional notes about the ingredient.

baseUnitOfMeasure.description: The standard unit of measure for this ingredient (e.g., 'gram', 'liter', 'piece'), used for consistency across the application.

currentBulkPrice.description: The current unit price of the ingredient when purchased in bulk.

currentRetailPrice.description: The current unit price of the ingredient when purchased at retail.

lastPriceUpdateDate.description: The date and time when the current bulk and retail prices were last updated.

Recipe.title: Recipe
Recipe.description: Defines a culinary recipe, including its name, description, and the quantity it yields.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Recipe entity.

name.description: The name of the recipe (e.g., 'Jollof Rice', 'Efo Riro').

description.description: A detailed description or cooking instructions for the recipe.

yieldQuantity.description: The quantity produced by following this recipe (e.g., 4 servings, 1000 grams).

yieldUnitOfMeasure.description: The unit of measure for the recipe's yield (e.g., 'servings', 'grams', 'portions').

RecipeIngredient.title: RecipeIngredient
RecipeIngredient.description: Links a specific ingredient to a recipe, specifying the exact quantity and unit of measure required for that recipe.

id.description: Unique identifier for the RecipeIngredient entity.

recipeId.description: Reference to the Recipe this ingredient is part of. (Relationship: Recipe 1:N RecipeIngredient)

ingredientId.description: Reference to the Ingredient used in this recipe. (Relationship: Ingredient 1:N RecipeIngredient)

quantity.description: The quantity of the ingredient required for this recipe.

unitOfMeasure.description: The unit of measure for the ingredient's quantity in this specific recipe (e.g., 'grams', 'pieces', 'ml'). This may differ from the ingredient's base unit if conversions are handled.

MarketPriceLog.title: MarketPriceLog
MarketPriceLog.description: Records historical bulk and retail prices for an ingredient at a specific date, supporting trend analysis and 'Weekly Market Price Update' functionality.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MarketPriceLog entity.

ingredientId.description: Reference to the Ingredient whose prices are being logged. (Relationship: Ingredient 1:N MarketPriceLog)

recordedDate.description: The date and time when these market prices were recorded.

bulkPrice.description: The bulk unit price of the ingredient recorded on this date.

retailPrice.description: The retail unit price of the ingredient recorded on this date.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to adhere strictly to the core principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Access Modeling, ensuring a secure, scalable, and easily debuggable system for EkoPlateCost. The central strategy revolves around a path-based ownership model, where all data belonging to a specific user (representing a restaurant) is nested under a dedicated path: `/users/{userId}/`. This approach intrinsically denormalizes the authorization context, placing the owner's UID directly into the document path.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** Authorization independence is achieved by embedding the `userId` directly into the path of all top-level collections (Ingredients, Recipes) and their respective subcollections (RecipeIngredients, MarketPriceLogs). For example, `users/{userId}/ingredients/{ingredientId}`. This design eliminates the need for `get()` calls in Firestore security rules to determine ownership. Instead, rules can directly compare `request.auth.uid` with the `{userId}` wildcard in the path (e.g., `request.auth.uid == userId`). This ensures atomic operations, simplifies rule logic, and prevents security vulnerabilities arising from complex hierarchical lookups.

**QAPs (Secure List Operations):** The structure inherently supports Query Authorization Principles by providing a secure `list` operation model. Because all user-specific data is strictly segregated under `/users/{userId}/`, any `list` query issued by a client will automatically be scoped to the data owned by the authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`). For instance, a query to fetch all ingredients will target `/users/{request.auth.uid}/ingredients`, and the security rules will only permit access if `request.auth.uid` matches the `userId` in the path. This means that rules do not act as filters; rather, the data's physical location (its path) combined with simple rules ensures that users can only query and retrieve data they are authorized to access, without exposing unauthorized data.

**Structural Segregation:** Each collection (`ingredients`, `recipes`, `recipeIngredients`, `marketPriceLogs`) maintains a homogeneous security posture, as all documents within a given user's scope (`/users/{userId}/...`) are accessible only by that user. There is no mixing of public and private data within the same collection. This simplifies security rules and makes their intent explicit.

**Access Modeling:** The chosen access model is Private Data via Path-Based ownership, leveraging Hierarchical Paths for User-Owned Data. All entities (Ingredient, Recipe, RecipeIngredient, MarketPriceLog) are directly owned by the user (`userId`) and nested accordingly. Wildcards are descriptive (`userId`, `ingredientId`, `recipeId`, `recipeIngredientId`, `marketPriceLogId`), enhancing clarity and predictability. No explicit global roles or collaborative data models are required based on the current application features, further simplifying the design.
